title: How the quadrille was danced
summary: She explains the quadrille: four couples facing, with several parts, and its relation to the contredance.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: I was wondering about any of the other dances,
the quadrilles. Did you ever dance any quadrilles when you were young?
Oh, yes. When I'd go to the dances, you know. We didn't call it dance. They didn't call them dance. They called them ball.
When you danced the quadrilles, what sort of parts did it have? Did it have four different parts?
Yeah, well, there'd be four on each side.
Did you call it a contradance?
No, no, not contradance. Well, maybe the Cajun called it contradance. Oh, I see.
Is the quadrille a kind of contradance? What do you mean by contradance when you use the word?
Oh, the quadrille, you see, we danced facing. It was really pretty.
Did you, well, was there one set of steps for the whole dance or were there different sections?
No, you see, four would get there, a man and the lady, and two there and two there, you see, and facing, like I'm facing you. Yes. That would be the same.
And they had two, three, four parts in the quadrille.
Four parts. Four parts, yeah. You danced the real French by the way. Yeah.
Yeah. There's what, was it pantalon was one section? Is that right?
